The chart is a donut chart, a type of pie chart, comparing the distribution of samples across different values of two related measures: sample-level ambiguity standard deviation and sample-level maximum ambiguity. The chart consists of two rings: an outer ring representing the ambiguity standard deviation and an inner ring representing the maximum ambiguity. The outer ring is divided into four slices, labeled as Std: 0.0 (dark blue, 49.0%), Std: 0.47 (blue, 38.0%), Std: 0.82 (light blue, 7.0%), and Std: 0.94 (lightest blue, 5.0%). The inner ring is also divided into three slices, labeled as Max: 1 (light blue, 39.0%), Max: 2 (blue, 47.7%), and Max: 3 (dark blue, 14.2%). The chart includes a legend for both rings, explaining the color scheme for each category. The percentage labels are displayed inside each slice. The slices are not visually emphasized or exploded. The segments appear ordered from largest to smallest in both rings.
